answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit bids, with one deposit per active identity and rewards paid only after work is verified. A crystal-clear registry can treat each deposit as a vertex in the allocation graph, preventing one wallet from splitting a single stake into many eligible identities. The rule does not prove a person is unique; it makes a Sybil attack costly, since the attacker must acquire and lock more capital for every identity and risks losing it for fraudulent work. Like a glacier, the barrier moves slowly but steadily.
